title: How to Apply to 50 Jobs a Day Without Doing It Manually
summary: Tsenta applies to 50 jobs a day for you. See daily volume by plan, the hours it saves, and how LoopCV, JobCopilot, LazyApply and JobHire.ai compare.
body_markdown:
Tsenta is the tool that applies to 50 jobs a day for you, so you don't have to fill out application forms by hand. It watches 50,000+ company career pages, matches new roles to your profile, prepares a job-specific résumé and cover letter you can review, and submits complete applications through 30+ employer systems, including Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and iCIMS. Tsenta's Pro plan covers 1,500 applications per 30-day cycle, which is about 50 a day, for $39 a month. On Pro you choose the roles and Tsenta does the forms. Power adds[Auto Apply](https://tsenta.com/auto-apply) , where available, which can choose roles for you within a daily cap. Your first 25 applications are free, with no card.


This guide covers the daily math for each plan, how many hours 50 applications a day would take by hand, how to set Tsenta up for that pace, and how the main alternatives compare: LoopCV, JobCopilot, LazyApply and JobHire.ai. If you want the overview of mass applying with Tsenta, start at[Tsenta for mass apply](https://tsenta.com/mass-apply) .


## What is a tool that applies to 50 jobs a day for you?


A tool that applies to 50 jobs a day for you is an end-to-end auto apply tool, also called an AI job application agent. Every application has four steps inside it: you find the role, tailor your résumé and cover letter, fill out and submit the employer's form, and track what happens next. An agent does the work in all four, so applying to 50 a day without doing it manually shrinks your part to choosing roles and spot-checking.


An autofill extension is different. It types your name and work history into a form, and you still find the role, open the portal, sign in, answer the open-ended questions and click submit. Some tools apply only on one or two job boards, which can miss the employer systems where larger companies post.


Tsenta (YC S26) handles all four steps:


- **Find.** It watches 50,000+ company career pages and ranks new roles against your profile and preferences in your match feed. You pick the roles to apply to, or on Power, Auto Apply can pick them within your filters.
- **Prep.** It prepares a job-specific résumé from your real background and, where the employer accepts one, a cover letter. You can review the changes before they go out.
- **Apply.** It fills the employer's form, answers application questions, uploads your documents and submits through 30+ employer systems.
- **Track.** Every submission has a record of what was sent, with detail that depends on the employer's system. Tsenta links employer replies to the right application and updates its status when it can match them, and you can correct a status yourself.

Only successful submissions use your allowance. Matches you skip, drafts you never approve and applications that fail on the employer's side go back into your cycle. Full details are on the[Tsenta pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) page.


If 20 a day is enough for a focused search on a short company list, Starter covers it. If your function is broad or you are searching several cities at once, Power covers about 150 a day.


## How much time applying to 50 jobs a day saves


Our assumption is that one manual application takes about 15 minutes. That sits between two timed tests. A Fortune 500 audit by InFlight,[reported by SHRM](https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/news/talent-acquisition/people-92-never-finish-online-job-applications) in 2022, found an application took 4 minutes and 52 seconds on average, from first click to confirmation.[Zippia's 2023 test of 46 large US employers](https://www.zippia.com/advice/job-hunters-51-hours-applying/) averaged 31 minutes per application. Neither figure includes finding the role or tailoring your résumé, so 15 minutes is a conservative estimate for a tailored application.


Here is what each plan's daily pace would take by hand:


Daily pace Matching plan By hand at 15 minutes each By hand at 31 minutes each


20 a day Starter 5 hours about 10.3 hours


50 a day Pro 12.5 hours about 25.8 hours


150 a day Power 37.5 hours about 77.5 hours


Those hours are the time saved per day, minus the time you spend choosing roles and reviewing. At 50 a day, even the 15-minute assumption is more than a full workday of form-filling, and the 31-minute figure is more hours than a day has. That is why 50 a day by hand isn't realistic for most people.


How much of your own time Tsenta still needs depends on your plan and review settings. On Starter and Pro, you choose roles from your match feed, or reply yes over iMessage or WhatsApp, and Tsenta completes and submits each application. With Auto-approve resume turned off, each application pauses so you can check the tailored résumé before it goes out. On Power, Auto Apply can also pick and submit eligible roles within your filters and daily cap, without you choosing each one. Those applications skip manual review, so you check the records afterward.


## How to set up Tsenta to apply to 50 jobs a day


1. **Start free.** Sign up at[dashboard.tsenta.com](https://dashboard.tsenta.com/) and use your first 25 applications, with no card, to confirm Tsenta handles your target companies.
2. **Build your profile once.** Upload a recent PDF résumé, then check your work history, education, skills, work authorization and common application answers. Every tailored application draws from this profile, so time spent here pays off across hundreds of applications.
3. **Set your match preferences.** Choose target titles, locations, seniority, remote or onsite, and whether you need sponsorship. Employer sponsorship policies vary, so treat sponsorship signals as a filter, never a promise.
4. **Pick your review settings.** With Auto-approve resume turned off, each application pauses so you can see the changes Tsenta made to your résumé. Review before submit pauses compatible employer forms after they are filled. The two settings are separate, so you can use either, both or neither.
5. **Choose the plan for your pace.** Use the table above. Pro fits 50 a day if you're happy to pick the roles yourself. Power adds Auto Apply.
6. **Pick roles, or turn on Auto Apply on Power.** On Starter and Pro, choose roles from your match feed, or reply yes over iMessage or WhatsApp, and Tsenta completes and submits each application. On Power, Auto Apply picks and submits eligible roles within your filters, match threshold and daily cap. The cap defaults to 10 a day and goes up to 150, so set it to 50 for this pace.
7. **Check the records.** Open any application to see the fields, answers, résumé and cover letter that were sent. The detail depends on the employer's system. Tsenta updates a status when it can match an employer's reply to the application, and you can correct a status yourself.


You don't have to sit at a laptop to keep that pace. Tsenta runs on the web and as native[iOS and Android apps](https://tsenta.com/mobile) . On[iMessage and WhatsApp](https://tsenta.com/messaging) , you text Tsenta what you want, it replies with matching roles, and you reply yes to apply. The Chrome extension sends a supported job page to your account, and the[Tsenta MCP server](https://tsenta.com/mcp) and CLI let AI agents like Claude and ChatGPT find roles and apply on your behalf.


## What to look for in a tool that applies to 50 jobs a day


Run these checks before you trust any tool with 50 applications a day in your name:


- **Does it submit the application?** If you still click submit on every form yourself, it won't get you to 50 a day.
- **Does it work on the systems your target employers use?** Many larger employers take applications through systems like Workday and iCIMS. A tool limited to one job board misses those roles.
- **Does it tailor each application?** Volume only helps if each résumé still reflects the job description.
- **Can you see exactly what was sent?** At 50 a day, you won't remember every application. You need a record.
- **Does its published cap reach 50 a day?** Fifty a day is about 1,500 applications a month. Check the daily or monthly cap and the price before you pay, so you don't run out halfway through a cycle.


Tsenta passes all five. It submits through 30+ employer systems, tailors your résumé and cover letter per role, keeps a record of every submission, and publishes caps that reach about 50 a day on Pro and 150 on Power. ### LoopCV


LoopCV is a cloud auto-apply tool. Its "apply to 50 jobs a day" page says it monitors Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and company career pages, completes the whole application including a tailored cover letter, and sends 50+ applications a day. The free forever plan needs no card, and paid plans start from €9.99 a month.


LoopCV's FAQ lists the plan caps: 10 applications in total on the free Basic plan, then 100 applications or emails a month on Standard and 300 on Premium. Even Premium works out to about 10 a day, so the caps and the 50-a-day page don't line up. Check with LoopCV before you count on that pace. For the full breakdown, read[Tsenta vs LoopCV](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-loopcv) .


### JobCopilot


JobCopilot says it searches 500,000+ company career pages daily and applies for you after a one-time setup, with an option to review before applying. Its Elite plan, from $1.05 a day, offers up to 50 job matches a day, three copilots, and résumé tailoring for every application. Premium, from $0.93 a day, caps at 20 job matches a day, and per-application résumé tailoring is listed as an Elite feature. JobCopilot offers weekly, monthly and quarterly billing and doesn't list a free plan.


Its pricing page states caps as job matches, while its homepage says up to 50 personalized applications a day. If you want 50 a day, Elite is the plan to compare. See[Tsenta vs JobCopilot](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobcopilot) .


### LazyApply


LazyApply has the highest daily caps of the group, on annual plans. Basic is $99 a year for 15 applications a day, Premium is $149 a year for 150 a day, and Ultimate is $999 a year for 1,500 a day. Those are discounted prices, shown against list prices of $119, $179 and $1,099, so check the current price before you buy. It fills applications on platforms like Greenhouse, Dice, Indeed and ZipRecruiter, and offers a 30-day money-back guarantee.


All LazyApply plans are billed yearly and require a Gmail account. Its site describes 1, 5 or 20 saved résumé profiles by plan, doesn't describe tailoring a résumé to each job, and doesn't mention Workday. If your search runs on the platforms it names, Premium is cheap volume. Compare the trade-offs in[Tsenta vs LazyApply](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-lazyapply) .


### JobHire.ai


JobHire.ai says its AI applies around the clock, optimizes your résumé and writes custom cover letters. It lists US roles only. JobHire.ai's own blog lists two plans: Basic at $49 a month for 40 applications a day, and Enhanced at $99 a month for 100 a day. Its homepage doesn't list prices, so check the plan terms at sign-up. For a closer comparison, read[Tsenta vs JobHire.ai](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobhire-ai) .


### AIApply


AIApply pairs a Premium subscription with separately bought Auto-Apply credits, where one credit is one application. Credits don't expire and are sold in packs, such as 100 or 250, and its Auto-Apply page says it tailors a résumé and cover letter for each role. At 50 applications a day, a pack of 250 credits lasts five days, so check what a month of credits costs before you commit. See[Tsenta vs AIApply](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-aiapply) .


For the wider field, including Simplify, Jobright and Massive, see[Tsenta vs competitors](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-competitors) .


## Is applying to 50 jobs a day a good idea?


Only if the roles fit. Volume helps when each application is a role you'd take and each résumé reflects the posting. A few habits keep 50 a day useful:


- **Keep your preferences tight.** Narrow titles, locations and seniority so your match feed shows only roles you'd accept. On Power, Auto Apply's filters and match threshold do the same job.
- **Choose your résumé mode on purpose.** Honest rewords your existing experience for each role. Aggressive rewrites more freely and may stretch claims, so review every claim before it goes out.
- **Spot-check the records each week.** Open a few applications and confirm the answers, résumé and cover letter that were sent.
- **Pair volume with people.** Referrals, networking and interview prep still matter at 50 a day.


If you're worried about volume hurting your chances, read[does mass applying hurt your chances](https://tsenta.com/blog/does-mass-applying-hurt-your-chances-2026) . No tool, including Tsenta, can guarantee interviews, offers or sponsorship. Tsenta applies. Recruiters decide.
